day_shape: 73 items: US Treasury authorises Iranian oil sales and dollar payments under newly finalised US-Iran MOU, Rubio departs for UAE/Kuwait/Bahrain to sell the deal, Ghalibaf meets Oman's Sultan on Strait of Hormuz, Khamenei lists 7 conditions, two UK parliamentary questions on Iran tabled.

threads.label: US-Iran MOU and oil sanctions waiver
threads.summary: The US Treasury authorised production, delivery and sale of Iranian oil, payments in dollars and US imports of Iranian petroleum, implementing the MOU finalised last week. Iran's Deputy FM Gharibabadi said technical talks in Switzerland concluded successfully, and VP Vance said Iran agreed to nuclear inspections among MOU conditions.

threads.label: Rubio Gulf tour and regional diplomacy
threads.summary: The State Department announced Secretary Rubio will travel to the UAE, Kuwait and Bahrain from 23-25 June to discuss the Iran MOU, Strait of Hormuz transit and regional priorities. The Jerusalem Post framed the trip as promoting the Iran deal amid Gulf concerns about Tehran's regional influence.

threads.label: Tehran reactions and Khamenei's conditions
threads.summary: Khamenei's office published seven conditions from the Islamabad memorandum, including cessation of military operations, lifting the naval blockade and affirmation of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Ministry spokesman Bagheri said Iran's missile capabilities are non-negotiable and denied meeting IAEA's Grossi, while Iran International reported hardliner manoeuvres in parliament.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz shipping confusion
threads.summary: IRIB said Ghalibaf met Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq in Muscat on arrangements for managing the Strait of Hormuz. Iran International cited the Financial Times reporting shipowners face conflicting Iran, US and western insurer guidance on Gulf transit routes.

threads.label: Israeli reception of US-Iran deal
threads.summary: A Jerusalem Post-cited Agam Institute/Hebrew University survey found a majority of Israelis view the MOU as a win for Tehran and a loss for Israel's long-term security. Trump allies defended the president to Israelis, while commentary debated implications for Israeli elections and Mossad chief Roman Gofman's appointment.

threads.label: Lebanon track and Hezbollah disarmament
threads.summary: Qatar and Pakistan announced a Lebanon deconfliction mechanism, and Israeli and Lebanese delegations are set to meet in Washington on Hezbollah disarmament and normalisation. Netanyahu, Katz, Zamir and Northern Command chief Milo issued a joint statement vowing continued IDF action in southern Lebanon; Defa Press cited Lebanon's Health Ministry putting casualties at 4,175 killed.

threads.label: Gaza operations and Hamas diplomacy
threads.summary: The IDF said it has expanded operational control to approximately 70% of the Gaza Strip and announced the killing of Nukhba operative Sabai Zaher Abd al-Hamid Abu Hasna, who held hostage Omer Shem Tov. The Jerusalem Post reported a "top secret" Hamas-French meeting on Palestinian affairs and 1967 borders, the first with European officials since October 7.

events.summary_en: The key to Washington in the hands of socialist Democrats. The decisive victory of Janice Lewis-George in the primary elections in Washington, the US capital, led it after 12 years towards a historic shift to the left and marked a major step by socialist Democrats to capture key city halls in the country. The US capital, after 12 years under the management of the technocratic and market-oriented Muriel Bowser, achieved a historic and structural shift to the left with the decisive victory of Janice Lewis-George in the Democratic primary elections. This victory, which effectively clears the path for her to take the seat of Washington's mayor, is the latest and most significant step by America's left-wing faction and members of Democratic Socialists.

events.title_en: A clan with 5 martyrs from Minaab School.
events.summary_en: A clan with 5 martyrs from Minaab School. In Minaab, a clan lives that lost 5 of their dear ones in the missile attack on the Shajara Tayyiba school complex; 3 students and 2 teachers. Fatima Karimi, mother of Saleh Abbasi, with tearful but proud eyes says: The enemy has left 5 wounds on our hearts. My son Saleh, along with my cousin's son, Sepehr Karimi, was martyred from Rahepaian Persian Gulf School. Another wound is Hananeh Zakeri, my aunt's granddaughter. Elham Karimi, deputy headmistress, and her sister Ansieh Karimi, sixth-grade teacher, both were my cousin girls and like my sister. Elham was the wife of my male cousin and Ansieh was my brother-in-law's wife. Both were martyred.

events.title: Federal Acquisition Regulation: Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul Parts 1, 2, 4, 33, 39, 40, and 53
events.summary: OFPP, DoD, GSA, and NASA (collectively referred to as the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council or FAR Council) are proposing to amend the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) to implement Executive Order (E.O.) 14275, Restoring Common Sense to Federal Procurement. The E.O. directs the elimination of excessive acquisition regulations to stop the inefficient use of American taxpayer dollars. The FAR Council is issuing twelve proposed rules that collectively will streamline the FAR in its entirety. This rule proposes revisions to FAR parts 1, 2, 4, 33, 39, 40, 52, and 53.
